truthset_standard: Synthetic: 150 designed fusions (80 intact-exon + 70 broken-exon) simulated with the EricScript simulator/wgsim, with and without real-tissue background reads; Real: experimentally verified fusions reported by the source studies (27 breast cancer cell lines [Edgren 2011], 11 melanoma [Berger 2010], 12 prostate cancer [Yu 2014]); Validation: 9 synthetic spike-in fusion transcripts (SRR1659964, Tembe 2014). "only a small set of validated fusion transcripts was available" (Methods, Precision-recall plot).
experimentally_validated: No (legacy-based; real-data truth = previously published validated fusions); synthetic truth for simulated sets; spike-in truth for validation set
notes: Moderately trusted, widely reused (Edgren TP27 reused); plus simulated and spike-in truth | new_tool_annotation (extraction): partial: FusionMetaCaller (rank-sum meta-caller of SOAPfuse+FusionCatcher+JAFFA) proposed; meta-caller results figure-only (Fig 7-8, Supp Fig S11-S13), not extracted
preprocessing: "we adopted the most recent versions in May 2015 and used the default alignment settings in each of the 15 pipelines ... (except that we fine-tuned the parameters of TopHat-Fusion)"; minimum spanning reads >=3, split reads >=1, anchor >=10 bp, 1 mismatch per 25 bp where configurable (Methods; Supp Tables S2, S7, S8)
reproducibility: Tool versions (Supp Table S2) and key parameters (Supp Tables S7-S8) reported; synthetic data generation described but simulated reads/truth files not deposited; real data from public sources; no benchmarking code, workflow or container; FusionMetaCaller R package at http://tsenglab.biostat.pitt.edu/software.htm (host did not resolve on 2026-11-17).
code_available: Yes (tool only; meta-caller R package, link currently unreachable)

truthset_standard: Spike-in: synthetic fusion RNAs of known identity and amount spiked into cell-line RNA (sensitivity); precision assessed against spike-ins plus an imputed truth (i-Truth) of 48 background fusions predicted by consensus of submitted entries ("we estimated a set of 'imputed truth' (i-Truth) fusions from the calls made by the entries"); simulated rnaseqSim tumours for preliminary rounds; GIAB sample as null model.
experimentally_validated: Partly: spike-in constructs are known by design (verified by IGV inspection of junction reads); i-Truth not experimentally validated (44/48 database-supported, >=3 literature-validated)
notes: Hybrid truth: designed spike-ins + consensus-imputed background fusions (wisdom-of-crowds component); consider new category "spike-in + consensus" | new_tool_annotation (extraction): no (community challenge; organizer-run blinded evaluation of team-submitted CWL/Docker workflows; Arriba and STAR-Fusion entries submitted by their developers)
preprocessing: Each entry ran its own CWL v1.0 workflow and Docker image with participant-chosen parameters on GRCh37.75 reference; organizers executed all entries on ISB-CGC (n1-standard-16, up to n1-highmem-16; 35 h limit); max 3 scored entries per team
reproducibility: All leaderboard entries available as CWL workflows (https://github.com/smc-rna-challenge) with Docker images (https://quay.io/organization/smc-rna-challenge); evaluation and figure code at https://github.com/smc-rna-challenge/SMC-RNA-Eval; spike-in FASTQs on Synapse syn22344794; simulator https://github.com/Sage-Bionetworks/rnaseqSim
tool_versions_reported: partial (embedded in per-entry CWL/Docker; not tabulated)
parameters_disclosed: Yes (encoded in per-entry CWL workflows; Table S10 lists filters of top-2 entries)
